_fixture: RETURNS_ORDER_ADMIN_073 — Swagger-shaped create body for POST /api/order/customerOrders. The DEDICATED disposable order of the legacy Admin SPA returns suite 073 (More > Returns > Add new return > Customer orders picker > Make return). Completed, fully delivered today, TWO eligible lines ordered 20 and 25.
_why: Before this fixture, 073 live-discovered the first order in the picker not prefixed AGENT-TEST-ORD-RET- and so created returns against REAL orders of human testers. Every 073 case that creates a return now picks THIS order by its number. Two lines, because the picker defaults Quantity to the full returnable quantity of a line, so a case whose Cleanup (set the return Cancelled) was skipped holds a whole line; the second line is the margin. Depth, because some cases type a quantity of 1; td:validate:orders FAILS when either line is ordered fewer units than the number of 073 rows that consume this alias. The two quantities differ so a clamped-back-to-N reading names its line.
_contract: Every `_`-prefixed key is FIXTURE METADATA, stripped by the seeder before the POST. Line identity comes from live discovery; delivery dates come from `_deliveryOffsetDays` resolved against seed-time now. There is NO literal date and NO runtime GUID in this file — the created order id, its line item ids and the resolved delivery instants are written to test-data/aliases.<env>.json.
_seedPhases: PHASE 1 POST creates the order (the platform ASSIGNS line item ids and IGNORES client-supplied ones, so shipment items cannot be linked at create). PHASE 2 PUT stamps shipments[].items[] with the assigned lineItemId + the inline lineItem object (without the inline object the platform silently drops the shipment item) and the shipment deliveryDate. Line order is NOT preserved by the platform, so lines are matched by SKU, never by index.
